{{nihongo|'''Wakeoe Shrine'''|別小江神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Yasui 4-chōme, {{ill|Kita-ku, Nagoya|Q1207964|qid=Q1207964|lt=Kita-ku}}, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It has been identified with "Wakeoe Shrine" of Yamada District, Owari Province, in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' but there are differing views as described below. {{nihongo|'''Wakeoe Shrine'''|別小江神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== History ==
Until the {{ill|Edo period|lt=Edo period|qid=Q184963}} it was called '''Rokusho Daimyōjin''' and was the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of Yasui village in {{ill|Kasugai district|Q11513576|qid=Q11513576}}. The early-Edo '{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}' records "Yasui village ... Rokusho Daimyōjin ... previously tax-exempt." At that time, the Inagaki family served as {{ill|Kannushi (disambiguation)|Q15888735|qid=Q15888735}}. Founding date is unknown. One theory says it originally stood at Senbonsugi to the northeast and was moved to the current site in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 12 ({{ill|1584|ab|1584|af|1584|als|1584|am|1584 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1584|ar|1584|ary|1584|arz|1584|ast|1584|avk|1584|az|1584|azb|۱۵۸۴ (میلادی)|bar|1584|bcl|1584|be|1584|be_x_old|1584|bg|1584|bn|১৫৮৪|bpy|মারি ১৫৮৪|br|1584|bs|1584.|ca|1584|cdo|1584 nièng|ceb|1584|ckb|١٥٨٤|crh|1584|cs|1584|cv|1584|cy|1584|da|1584|de|1584|diq|1584|el|1584|eml|1584|eo|1584|es|1584|et|1584|eu|1584|fa|۱۵۸۴ (میلادی)|fi|1584|fo|1584|fr|1584|frr|1584|fur|1584|fy|1584|ga|1584|gan|1584年|gcr|1584|gd|1584|gl|1584|gv|1584|he|1584|hi|१५८४|hr|1584.|ht|1584 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1584|hy|1584|hyw|1584 թուական|ia|1584|id|1584|ilo|1584|io|1584|is|1584|it|1584|ja|1584年|jv|1584|ka|1584|kaa|1584|kk|1584 жыл|ko|1584년|krc|1584 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1584|la|1584|lb|1584|lij|1584|lld|1584|lmo|1584|lt|1584 m.|lv|1584. gads|mai|१५८४|map_bms|1584|mdf|1584|mg|1584|mhr|1584|mi|1584|mk|1584|mr|इ.स. १५८४|mrj|1584 и|ms|1584|my|၁၅၈၄|myv|1584 ие|mzn|۱۵۸۴|nah|1584|nap|1584|nds|1584|new|सन् १५८४|nl|1584|nn|1584|no|1584|nrm|1584|nso|1584|oc|1584|olo|1584|or|୧୫୮୪|os|1584-æм аз|pl|1584|pnb|1584|pt|1584|qu|1584|ro|1584|ru|1584 год|rue|1584|sa|१५८४|sah|1584|sc|1584|scn|1584|sd|1584ع|se|1584|sh|1584.|shn|1584|simple|1584|sk|1584|sl|1584|smn|1584|sq|1584|sr|1584|su|1584|sv|1584|sw|1584|ta|1584|tg|Соли 1584|th|พ.ศ. 2127|tk|1584|tl|1584|tly|1584|tr|1584|tt|1584 ел|uk|1584|ur|1584ء|uz|1584|vec|1584|vi|1584|vls|1584|wa|1584|war|1584|wuu|1584年|xmf|1584|yi|1584|zh|1584年|zh_min_nan|1584 nî|zh_yue|1584年|qid=Q6728}}) by order of {{ill|Oda Nobukatsu|Q3044815|qid=Q3044815}}, while another says shrine buildings had long stood around the present site because remains of dead Senbonsugi trees are within the precinct{{Sfn|加藤宏|1988|p=281}}. It is said to have lost part of shrine lands due to Bizen land surveys in the {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} period{{Sfn|愛知県西春日井郡|1988|p=323}}. In early {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} it was renamed "Wakeoe Shrine." It was burned in the {{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} air raids ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 20) but rebuilt in {{ill|1966|Q2649|qid=Q2649}} (Shōwa 41)<ref name="歴史" />.

The Hachiman shrine merged here, also called "Enna Hachiman" or "Engi Hachiman," is said to have originally stood in the same precinct{{Sfn|愛知県西春日井郡|1988|p=323}}. According to shrine tradition, it was founded at Senbonsugi in the era of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|Q314802|qid=Q314802}}, but was heavily damaged by flood in {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|Q1193577|qid=Q1193577}} 17 ({{ill|1520|Q6284|qid=Q6284}}){{Sfn|愛知県西春日井郡|1988|p=323}}. It is said Asano Matazaemon Nagakatsu rebuilt it in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 11 ({{ill|1583|Q6726|qid=Q6726}}), and a ridge tag from that time reportedly reads: "Tenshō 11 ... invited Hachiman-sha ... shrine official Inagaki Udayū Fujiwara Yasuo ... built by Asano Hachirōzaemon, nephew of Asano Nagamasa, descendant of Genji of Hachiman"{{Sfn|愛知県西春日井郡|1988|p=323}}. However, Edo-period gazetteers do not describe this Hachiman shrine. It was formally merged in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 9 ({{ill|1920|Q2155|qid=Q2155}}) as a precinct shrine of Wakeoe Shrine{{Sfn|愛知県西春日井郡|1988|p=323}}.

The Yamada District "Wakeoe Shrine" in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' is the same as "Ōe Tenjin" in the '{{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|Q11041830|qid=Q11041830}}.' By the Edo period its location had become unknown; 'Owari Shinmeichō Shūsetsu no Teikō' states "this shrine's location is unknown now; later generations should examine," and '{{ill|Owarishi|Q137855962|qid=Q137855962}}' likewise says "Wakeoe Shrine appears in Engi Jinmyōshiki but present location is unclear." However, '{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}' identified Wakeoe Shrine with Rokusho Myōjin in Yasui village (this shrine).
{{Quotation|One theory says it is Suwa Shrine in Kamioda village, Kasugai District, but that is Kasugai District, not Yamada District, and lacking clear origin. In Yasui village, our province's divine-register has Ōe Tenjin, and local names such as Ōeyoshiyama and Senbonsugi provide one basis. Also, in an exemption document given by Asano Katsuyuki, father of Asano Nagamasa, to shrine official Inagaki when he worshiped Ōe Hachiman in this village, it says "Wakeoe Shrine ..." This too is sufficient evidence. For now, append this to reference.|'Tokusen Jinmyōchō,' Wakeoe Shrine}}

Thus 'Tokusen Jinmyōchō' identified this shrine based on place names like "Ōeyoshiyama" and the Asano document. But the authenticity of the latter {{ill|komonjo|Q89298567|qid=Q89298567}} has also been questioned<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%88%A5%E5%B0%8F%E6%B1%9F%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE-3064790|editor=Heibonsha|website=Kotobank|title=Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei "Wakeoe Shrine"|accessdate=2025-11-06}}</ref>. Also, the 1143 ({{ill|Kōji (Heian period)|Q1194459|qid=Q1194459}} 2) "Owari no Kuni Ajiki-shō Rikkenmon" lists "Yasui-ri" as a village-name within Ajiki-shō of Harube District, so Yasui is considered likely to have belonged to Harube, not Yamada, in the Heian period{{Sfn|「角川日本地名大辞典」編纂委員会|1989|p=1350}}.

== Notes ==
Long revered as deity of safe childbirth, children's protection, and longevity by figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}}, Tameyoshi-go, and successive Oda, Toyotomi, and Tokugawa leaders<ref name="歴史"/>. The "Meoto-sugi" pair in the precinct is a natural monument<ref name="歴史"/> and is said to be a city historic scenic site. Stones used for Kiyomasa Bridge, set on the Inaoki Road by {{ill|Katō Kiyomasa|Q1069843|qid=Q1069843}} during construction of {{ill|Nagoya Castle|Q648629|qid=Q648629}}, are said to remain in the precinct.
